rationale: Interpret receipt 5c818a5cd9f5483c9ba6aea7c62e074a, the second run of the lease window. The 500 ms lease failed at 507 ms and the 1 s lease at 1015 ms, against 510 ms and 1018 ms in the first run, so the bound is reproduced to within ten milliseconds and the account's explanation, counterevidence, gap answers and limitations stand as written. I added the receipt to the execution set and appended the parsed result to the rationale and the repeat to the joint history.

interpretations.rationale:
Conclusion: explained at the question level, with the scoped defect asserted and the receipts' comparisons recorded as violated. VerifyLeader reports success although the leader can reach fewer voters than the voter quorum it sized, because acknowledgements arriving on non-voter replication streams are counted as support. Evidence from receipt 7a54f3754b0b423aaf1ba6c0365367c0 (completed, tests_passed, exit 0). Parsed index 1, the trigger: five members were bootstrapped, two were demoted to non-voters, and the leader's transport was disconnected in both directions from the two remaining voters, so voters_reachable=1 against quorum_voters=2 while nonvoters_reachable=2; VerifyLeader completed with verify_ok=true and an empty error, and the node was still Leader. Parsed index 3, the control on an identically built cluster with the non-voters also disconnected (nonvoters_reachable=0): the same call completed with verify_ok=false and the error 'leadership lost while committing log', the node by then a Follower. The two cases differ only in whether the non-voters could answer, so the successful verification in the trigger is attributable to non-voter acknowledgements rather than to voter support. Mechanism from source: verifyLeader sets quorumSize with quorumSize(), which counts only voters (raft.go:1087-1100), but registers the verify future on every entry of leaderState.replState (raft.go:966-990), and startStopReplication creates a replication state for every configured server including non-voters (raft.go:583-600); any successful heartbeat or AppendEntries response calls notifyAll(true) (replication.go:100-112), which increments the verify future's vote count (future.go:274-293) and completes it at the voter-sized quorum. The library already uses the correct supporter set one function away: checkLeaderLease iterates the latest configuration and counts only voters (raft.go:1037-1050), so the two paths disagree about who can establish leadership. Consequence under the exercised conditions: a client that calls VerifyLeader to protect a read (api.go:927-931) is told the leader still holds a voter quorum while it can reach none of the other voters, so the guard against serving stale reads after leadership loss does not hold in a cluster that contains non-voters. A successor run, receipt e49121154f514e39b6c1a37a2c353a4a, repeated the call every 50 ms after the first verification and quantified the window: parsed index 1 again records verify_ok=true for the partitioned leader, and parsed index 2 records loop_successes=20 with ms_until_failure=1015 before the node became a Follower, so twenty separate verifications succeeded across about one second; the control at parsed index 4 recorded verify_ok=false and parsed index 5 recorded loop_successes=0 with failure at 0 ms. The false assurance therefore lasts for the leader lease interval (LeaderLeaseTimeout, one second in this harness), not for a single call. A clean-copy repeat of the same fixed experiment, receipt 13b7844febba4a6d80c7331818c943f6, reproduced the window: parsed index 1 verify_ok=true, parsed index 2 loop_successes=20 with ms_until_failure=1014, parsed index 4 verify_ok=false and parsed index 5 loop_successes=0. Both runs therefore agree on the count and on a window of about one second at this lease setting. End-to-end consequence, measured in receipt 27d9e2e68fcf4e15b00b170ef9593714 (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): five real nodes run as three voters and two non-voters with a recording state machine, the leader commits v1, is partitioned from the other two voters while the non-voters stay reachable, and is asked to verify itself immediately afterwards. Parsed index 0 records that state (voters_reachable=1, nonvoters_reachable=2, leader_value=v1); parsed index 1 records verify_after_partition_ok=true with ms_to_verify=0, so the false assurance is issued at once, but it also records ms_to_new_leader=2564 with new_leader_value=v2, verify_after_failover_ok=false and the error 'node is not the leader', old_value_before_heal=v1 against the successor's v2, and stale_verified_read=false. The old leader therefore stopped being able to verify itself before any successor had committed, so in this configuration the defect never became a verified stale read. Parsed index 3, the control with the non-voters also cut: verification failed after 1009 ms with 'leadership lost while committing log', and the successor committed v2 at 1476 ms, which shows the success in the trigger again depended on the non-voters while both cases ended with the old leader out of office. Second suffrage shape, receipt c211ca53de834d06a9b84e80fc18f1b7 (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): four members, one of them demoted, so the configuration has three voters and exactly one non-voter and the voter quorum is two. Parsed index 0 records voters_reachable=1, nonvoters_reachable=1, quorum_voters=2, demotion_converged=true and demotion_converge_ms=5, so the member whose acknowledgement is being counted had already applied its own demotion; parsed index 1 records verify_ok=true in 0 ms with the node still Leader, although it could reach only one of the two voters its sizing requires. Parsed index 3, the control with the single non-voter also cut: verify_ok=false after 50 ms with 'leadership lost while committing log', the node a Follower. One non-voter is therefore enough to supply the acknowledgement the voter quorum is missing, and the success ends as soon as that member is unreachable. Why the window closes is structural rather than lucky: this library rejects a configuration whose LeaderLeaseTimeout exceeds its HeartbeatTimeout, and requires HeartbeatTimeout <= ElectionTimeout, so a follower cannot begin an election before the old leader's lease has already run out, and the vote round trip only adds to that margin. The defect's practical reach is therefore a false leadership-health signal that lasts up to one lease interval, not a stale read after a failover. The membership document defines a non-voter as 'a server that receives log entries but is not considered for elections or commitment purposes' (membership.md:11-12), which supports treating a non-voter's acknowledgement as ineligible support for a leadership verification sized as a voter quorum.

Repeat of the end-to-end experiment, receipt fb14e70f60a3456eae7774eb6e005e69 (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): the same fixed inputs were run again. Parsed index 0 records the trigger's state with one of three voters and both non-voters reachable, and parsed index 1 its result: the leader verified itself at 0 ms after the partition, the successor was elected and applied the new value at 2373 ms, the old leader's own value was still the initial one before the heal, its later verification failed with 'node is not the leader', and no stale verified read was recorded. Parsed index 2 records the control's state with the non-voters unreachable as well, and parsed index 3 its result: verification failed after 994 ms with 'leadership lost while committing log', the successor applied the new value at 1917 ms, and again no stale verified read. The bound the account claims therefore reproduces on a second execution with a successor about 190 ms faster than in the first run, so the false success remains confined to the interval between the partition and the lease-driven step-down rather than being an artifact of one run's timing.

Lease variation, receipt 871eb51d712b4c269dd592937ab068f7 (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): the same five-member shape with two non-voters and the leader cut from the two remaining voters, run at two lease settings. Parsed index 0 records the 500 ms case with a 500 ms heartbeat and a 600 ms election timeout, and parsed index 1 its result: the first verification succeeded at 0 ms, ten consecutive verifications succeeded, the first failure came at 510 ms and the leader ended as a follower. Parsed index 2 records the 1 s case with a 1 s heartbeat and a 1 s election timeout, and parsed index 3 its result: the first verification succeeded at 0 ms, twenty consecutive verifications succeeded, the first failure came at 1018 ms and the leader again ended as a follower. The window therefore follows the configured lease across a factor of two, roughly 510 ms against 1018 ms, which replaces the earlier inference from a single setting, and the number of successes scales with it as well, ten against twenty at a fifty-millisecond interval.

Question-level consolidation after the premise correction. The verification entry now records that verifyLeader starts the count at one for the leader itself, sizes a voter-only quorum and registers the future on every replication stream. Read across both lineages that this account uses, that arithmetic explains every recorded outcome: in the five-member receipts the quorum is two, the leader supplies one vote and a single non-voter acknowledgement completes the verification, and the control with the non-voters also cut has no second acknowledgement and fails after about a second; in the lease receipts the same shape succeeds at the first attempt under both a 500 ms and a 1 s lease and then fails when the lease-driven step-down arrives, at 510 ms and 1018 ms; in the end-to-end receipts the same first verification succeeds at 0 ms while the successor commits only after about 2.4 seconds, and the later verification is refused because the node is no longer the leader. Nothing above depends on the leader being excluded from the count, so the correction sharpens the mechanism without changing the conclusion that the verification is satisfied without a second voter.

Repeat of the stale-read experiment, receipt e312b6dd60ec40869dff4f74d241bfa2 (completed, tests_passed, exit 0), which reruns 2fd5794c550141f7889f1530295d1294-experiment from its retained inputs. Parsed index 0 records the trigger with five members, three voters, one voter reachable and both non-voters reachable; parsed index 1 records its result: the verification after the partition succeeded in 0 ms with no error, the successor committed a different value and was elected at 2330 ms, the old leader had become a Follower holding the new value by the time it was measured, its later verification failed with 'node is not the leader', and no verified read was served from stale data. Parsed index 2 records the control with both non-voters cut, and parsed index 3 its result: the same verification failed after 1005 ms with 'leadership lost while committing log', the successor was elected at 2676 ms, and again no stale verified read occurred. The pair therefore reproduces on a second run with the same direction, the same zero-millisecond success in the trigger and the same refusal in the control, so the claim that non-voter acknowledgements complete a voter quorum in this three-voter shape does not rest on one execution; the recorded bound, that the false success lasts only until the lease check or the successor's election removes the leader, is also unchanged.

Repeat of the lease window, receipt 5c818a5cd9f5483c9ba6aea7c62e074a (completed, tests_passed, exit 0), from the same 64b6f78684b04f8ea393a5827f5457c7-experiment. Both cases first verified at 0 ms with one of three voters reachable and the non-voters answering, then lost leadership once the lease expired: the 500 ms case failed at 507 ms after ten loop successes and the 1 s case at 1015 ms after twenty, ending as Follower in both. The earlier run recorded 510 ms and 1018 ms, so the bound reproduces within ten milliseconds and the account's reading - that a false success buys one lease interval, not a durable assurance - now rests on two runs.

1e9081120a23413eaaf020fffb085a1b-gap-0.explanation: The current explanation and the lease experiment, both of which this question-level account carries, assert only that a verification succeeds while one of three voters is reachable and the non-voters answer. With the leader's self-vote recorded, that is exactly a quorum of two met by the leader plus one non-voter acknowledgement, so the affected uses are confirmed rather than revised; their recorded comparison results stay violated.

1e9081120a23413eaaf020fffb085a1b-gap-1.explanation: The end-to-end receipts from 2fd5794c550141f7889f1530295d1294-experiment, 27d9e2e68fcf4e15b00b170ef9593714 and its repeat fb14e70f60a3456eae7774eb6e005e69, are cited in this question-level record. They recorded a first verification succeeding at 0 ms under the same three-voter quorum, which the corrected premise explains the same way, and a later verification refused because the node had stepped down; neither observation depended on how the two votes were supplied, so those receipts need no reinterpretation and the bound they measured stands.

counterevidence: The verification returns before the lease check steps the leader down, so the false success is bounded by the leader lease interval rather than permanent; in the control that same step-down produced the error the trigger avoided. Receipt 27d9e2e68fcf4e15b00b170ef9593714 measures the bound directly: verification succeeded at 0 ms after the partition, the successor committed at 2564 ms, and the post-failover verification failed because the node was no longer the leader. The repeat, receipt fb14e70f60a3456eae7774eb6e005e69, measured the same shape: verification at 0 ms, the successor's commit at 2373 ms, and the later verification refused. Receipt 871eb51d712b4c269dd592937ab068f7 measured the same shape at two leases: the first failure came at 510 ms under a 500 ms lease and at 1018 ms under a 1 s lease, so the bound scales with the setting rather than being fixed.

VerifyLeader returning nil installed no leader and returned no data; the harm needs a client that relies on it as the guard the documentation describes. The end-to-end case issued a state-machine read after a later verification, and that verification failed, so no read was served under a false assurance.

Non-voter reachability does show the leader is alive and connected, so a deployment that used VerifyLeader only as a liveness probe would not be affected; the code sizes a voter quorum, which makes quorum the stated intent.
The partition was modelled by removing in-memory transport routing in both directions between the leader and the voters, not by dropping packets or crashing members.

The election that removes the false leader is not slowed down: in the end-to-end case the successors were elected 1.5 s and 2.6 s after the cut, while the lease expired after about 1 s, so neither case approached an overlap between a successful verification and a stale state machine.

In both suffrage shapes the successful verification was issued while the non-voters were reachable and stopped once they were cut, so the result is about which acknowledgements the call accepts, not about the size of the cluster.
limitations: Two suffrage shapes were exercised, both with three voters: five members with two non-voters and four members with one non-voter, each with the leader cut from the other voters. Larger clusters, configurations where non-voters outnumber voters, and a non-voter whose heartbeat is the only one in flight were not tested.

The end-to-end case reads the state machine directly rather than through a client read protocol, and its timing bound is configuration-specific: with a one-second lease and staggered election timeouts of 1.1 s, 2 s and 3 s the successors were elected at 2.6 s and 1.5 s. The library validates LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout <= ElectionTimeout, so a lease longer than an election is not expressible and the window cannot be widened that way; a slower election would widen the false-verification interval without changing the fact that the successor arrives after the lease. The repeat recorded successor commits at 2373 ms in the trigger and 1917 ms in the control, so the bound moved by a few hundred milliseconds between runs without changing the order of events.

The demotions completed before the partition in the single-non-voter case, where the demoted member's own view was read back and had converged in 5 ms; in the five-member receipts the members' views of the new configuration were not read back before the transport was cut.

The stale-read case covers one partition shape and one partition timing, applied after the leader has committed and settled. A partition that begins while a verification is already in flight, or a leader whose lease contact comes from a voter that is about to be deposed, was not exercised.

The exposure window is now measured at two lease settings, 500 ms and 1 s, and follows them; a 2 s setting was attempted and abandoned because the cluster helper's stability wait is shorter than the election timeout that setting implies, so the scaling above 1 s is untested, and every case keeps the non-voters reachable and the election timeout at or just above the lease.
